# Introduction {#sec-introduction}

```{=latex}
\IEEEPARstart{T}{his}
```
template combines an IEEE-compatible journal class with an editable Quarto
source. Write ordinary prose, headings, lists, equations, figures, tables,
cross-references, and citations in Markdown. Use raw LaTeX only for
class-specific structures such as the title block, `IEEEkeywords`, and author
biographies. A citation can be written as [@young1964].

## Abbreviations and Acronyms

Define abbreviations and acronyms when they first appear in the text, even if
they were already defined in the abstract. Avoid abbreviations in the title
unless they are unavoidable.

## Equations

Number equations consecutively and define every symbol near its first use. For
example,

$$
E = mc^2.
$$ {#eq-energy}

Refer to @eq-energy instead of typing a fixed equation number.

# Methods

Describe the data, experimental design, software, and statistical procedures
in enough detail for another researcher to reproduce the work. Use SI units
consistently and report uncertainty together with point estimates.

## Lists

The following is ordinary Markdown:

1. Define the research question.
2. Record data-processing rules.
3. Report software versions and parameters.

# Results

@fig-magnetization demonstrates a standard one-column figure. Keep
axis labels and annotations legible at the final printed size.

![Magnetization as a function of applied field. Explain the significance of
the figure in the caption.](image/fig1.png){#fig-magnetization fig-pos="t" width="100%"}

Table 1 demonstrates a compact one-column table. The IEEE two-column class is
not compatible with Pandoc's default `longtable` output, so tables use a small
raw LaTeX block.

```{=latex}
\begin{table}[!t]
\caption{Selected Magnetic Quantities and SI Units}
\label{tbl-units}
\centering
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
\begin{tabular}{cll}
\hline
Symbol & Quantity & Example SI unit \\
\hline
$B$ & magnetic flux density & T \\
$H$ & magnetic field strength & A/m \\
$m$ & magnetic moment & A$\cdot$m$^2$ \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

# Discussion

Interpret the results in relation to the study question and earlier work.
Separate direct evidence from speculation, describe limitations, and avoid
claims that extend beyond the design or data.

# Conclusion

Summarize the main result and its scope without repeating the abstract.

# Acknowledgment {.unnumbered}

The authors thank colleagues and facilities that contributed to this work.
Use the singular heading “Acknowledgment” in accordance with the source
template.
